input.quote: This Agreement and the license granted under this Agreement shall remain in effect perpetually as long as fees are paid by Sparkling in accordance with the Fee Schedule and the Agreement is not otherwise terminated in accordance with this Section.
input.rationale: Garman owns all IP in the Work, including the Improvements and the Schedule "D" Modifications we pay for (§13), while our only right is a non-exclusive licence capped to Authorized Locations (§2), expressly non-sublicensable (§3(c)) and lasting only while fees are paid and the Agreement is not terminated (§17(a)). That fails the fallback licence-back position on its material terms: the licence is neither perpetual nor irrevocable, is not worldwide or royalty-free (extra fees apply for other locations), and carries no right to modify or sublicense for our business. Nothing limits Garman's use of our converted data (§4(b)). We therefore target fallback: Vendor ownership of the Work is preserved (already met at §13); we add the four modifiers and the use/modify/sublicense rights, carve the Section 2 licence out of the §17(a) termination mechanic so perpetuity and irrevocability are not contradicted, delete only the conflicting sublicence bar, extend the grant to Improvements and Modifications, and keep "non-transferable" and the AS400 platform wording untouched.

proposal.summary: Make the §2 licence perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide and royalty-free with rights to use, modify and sublicense the Software (including Improvements and Modifications) and Documentation, conform §17(a) so that licence survives termination, conform the §3(c) sublicence bar, and limit Garman's use of our data to providing the services.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Garman keeps ownership of the Work, but our licence must be perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free and extend to modifying and sublicensing the Software (including Improvements and Modifications) and Documentation for our business, so we have removed the Authorized-Locations place-of-use cap and additional-fee sentence, carved the Section 2 licence out of the Section 17(a) termination mechanic so perpetuity is not contradicted, and deleted the conflicting sublicence bar in Section 3(c). We have also confirmed that any licence to Garman in our data is limited to processing it solely to provide the services.
